Vite Introduction.exp: Introduction to Vite and its ecosystem.

Project Setup: Vite scaffolds projects using create-vite with templates for vanilla JS/TS, React, Vue, Svelte, Lit, and more. The setup process installs dependencies and configures the build tool in seconds.

npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react
cd my-app
npm install
npm run dev
CLI Commands: Vite provides three primary CLI commands: vite (dev server), vite build (production build), and vite preview (preview production build). Flags like --port, --host, and --mode customize behavior.

vite --port 3000 --host 0.0.0.0  # Dev server on all interfaces
vite build --mode staging         # Build with staging env
Dev Server: Vite's dev server uses native ES modules and esbuild pre-bundling for instant startup. Hot Module Replacement updates modules without full page reloads, preserving application state during development.

Mode: Vite modes (development, production, custom) determine which .env files are loaded. Custom modes like staging or test use .env.staging or .env.test files for environment-specific configuration.
.env Files: Vite loads environment variables from .env files with specific priority: .env.[mode].local > .env.[mode] > .env.local > .env. Only variables prefixed with VITE_ are exposed to client code.

# .env.local
VITE_API_URL=https://api.example.com
VITE_APP_TITLE=My App
# Not exposed: SECRET_KEY=abc123
Import.meta.env: Environment variables are accessed via import.meta.env in client code. Vite also provides built-in variables like import.meta.env.MODE, import.meta.env.PROD, and import.meta.env.DEV.

Static Assets: Vite handles static assets (images, fonts, SVGs) as ES module imports. Assets smaller than a configurable threshold are inlined as base64 data URLs, while larger files are emitted as separate files.
PostCSS: Vite includes PostCSS support out of the box. A postcss.config.js file is automatically detected, enabling features like Tailwind CSS, Autoprefixer, and custom CSS transformations.
CSS Modules: CSS Modules are supported natively for files ending in .module.css. Class names are locally scoped by default, and the generated module object maps original class names to hashed versions.

Official: Vite's official plugins include @vitejs/plugin-react (with Fast Refresh), @vitejs/plugin-vue, @vitejs/plugin-svelte, and @vitejs/plugin-legacy for legacy browser support.
Community: The community ecosystem includes plugins for PWA (vite-plugin-pwa), SVG (vite-plugin-svg), compression (vite-plugin-compression), and more. Most popular frameworks have dedicated Vite plugins.
Custom Plugins: Custom Vite plugins follow the Rollup plugin convention with additional Vite-specific hooks. Plugins use the name, apply, enforce, and various transform/build hooks to modify behavior.

Server-Side Rendering: Vite provides SSR support with built-in APIs for development and production. The SSR build produces a server entry point that can render Vue/React components on the server.
SSR Build: The SSR build generates a separate bundle optimized for Node.js execution. It disables CSS extraction and produces ESM or CJS output depending on the configured format.

Webpack to Vite: Migrating from Webpack involves replacing loaders with Vite plugins, converting CommonJS to ESM, and adapting custom Webpack configurations to Vite's simpler config format. Most Webpack loaders have Vite equivalents.

# Install Vite and counterparts
npm uninstall webpack webpack-cli
npm install -D vite @vitejs/plugin-react
# Convert webpack.config.js to vite.config.js
CRA to Vite: Migrating from Create React App to Vite requires installing Vite, moving index.html to the root, replacing react-scripts with Vite scripts, and updating env variables from REACT_APP_ to VITE_.

npm uninstall react-scripts
npm install -D vite @vitejs/plugin-react
// package.json scripts
"dev": "vite",
"build": "vite build",
"preview": "vite preview"
// Rename REACT_APP_* to VITE_* in .env

Code Splitting: Vite automatically splits code into separate chunks for dynamic imports. Manual chunking can be configured in the build.rollupOptions to separate vendor libraries from application code.
Chunking: Advanced chunking strategies control how modules are grouped into output files. Vite supports async chunk loading, CSS code splitting, and granular control over chunk file names.
Production Build: The vite build command produces optimized assets for production. It bundles with Rollup, minifies with esbuild or terser, applies code splitting, and generates hashed filenames for caching.

Plugins: Plugins extend Vite's functionality using a Rollup-compatible plugin API. They can transform code, inject styles, optimize assets, and hook into the build lifecycle at various stages.
Resolve: The resolve config controls module resolution, including aliases, extensions, and main fields. Path aliases simplify imports by mapping @/ to the src directory.
vite.config.js: Vite is configured via vite.config.js using the defineConfig helper for type hints. The config file supports conditional configurations based on mode, environment, and build targets.

Vite Data.exp: Working with data and APIs in Vite.

Vite SSR & Library Mode: Vite supports Server-Side Rendering (SSR) for frameworks like Vue and React. SSR builds produce server and client entry points. vite-plugin-ssr and vite-node provide SSR tooling. Library mode (build.lib) packages components/libraries as ES modules, CommonJS, or UMD. Library entries: entry (main), name (global variable), formats (['es', 'cjs', 'umd']). dts plugin generates TypeScript declarations. vite-plugin-dts for library type generation. external marks peer dependencies as not bundled. CSS in libraries should use CSS modules or inline styles.
Build Optimization & Code Splitting: Vite uses Rollup for production builds with optimized defaults: CSS code splitting, async chunk loading, and automatic dependency pre-bundling. Configure build.rollupOptions for manual chunk splitting. manualChunks separates vendor code from app code. build.target sets ES target. build.minify uses esbuild (fast) or terser (more options). build.cssMinify for CSS minification. chunkSizeWarningLimit controls size warnings. Dynamic imports with import() create automatic split points. Visualize bundle with rollup-plugin-visualizer. Analyze with vite-bundle-visualizer.

Library Mode: Library mode builds your code as a reusable library instead of an app. Vite outputs ESM, CJS, and UMD formats with externalized dependencies and TypeScript declaration generation.
Web Workers: Vite supports web workers with a simple ?worker import suffix, automatically bundling worker scripts into separate chunks. Inline workers are bundled into the main file.
WebAssembly: Vite supports importing .wasm files directly as ES modules, initializing WebAssembly modules with automatic compilation and providing exported functions for use in application code.
Glob Imports: Glob imports with import.meta.glob load multiple modules from the filesystem dynamically, supporting eager loading, pattern matching, and import assertions for Markdown or JSON files.
Environment API: Vite 6's Environment API provides a programmatic interface for configuring multiple environments (client, server, edge) within the same config, each with its own plugins and resolve options.
